# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: MUTE

You hold the manual. You cannot speak, you never see the bomb, and you cannot touch it.

## Your channels

When you gesture, Deaf receives it.
You cannot speak.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
The light never holds. It changes every round, and it always walks the
same circle of three colours. What matters is what it shows at the
moment of the cut.

| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| green | blue |
| orange | yellow |
| white | green |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

I hold the defusal manual, which states that the bomb features a light cycling through three colors (green, orange, white) and that the correct wire to cut depends on the light color at the moment of cutting (green light -> blue wire; orange light -> yellow wire; white light -> green wire).

I cannot speak, only gesture, and Deaf is the only one who can see my gestures. However, Deaf cannot hear, and no communication protocol or gesture vocabulary has been established yet. A sign means nothing until it is given meaning, and since Deaf can speak aloud (reaching both me and Blind), Deaf needs to describe what is visible on the bomb and establish or invite a code system. Blind also needs to report what they can feel.

Since I have no established signs to convey the manual yet, I will wait for Blind and Deaf to speak in Round 1.

```
wait()
```

TURN 2
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
The light never holds. It changes every round, and it always walks the
same circle of three colours. What matters is what it shows at the
moment of the cut.

| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| green | blue |
| orange | yellow |
| white | green |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: I am Blind. I can cut wires 1, 2, or 3. Deaf cannot hear us, but Deaf can see the bomb and speak. When Deaf speaks the bomb details, check the manual. Since I cannot see your gestures, gesture the target wire to Deaf (☝ for 1, ✌ for 2, 🤟 for 3) so Deaf can speak it aloud for me to cut.
Deaf says: BOMB STATUS: Display is 0. Light is white. There are 3 wires: Wire 1 is green, Wire 2 is blue, Wire 3 is yellow. Mute: since Blind cannot see gestures and you cannot speak, gesture to me what Blind must do. For cutting wires: ☝ = Wire 1, ✌ = Wire 2, 🤟 = Wire 3. I will speak your instruction to Blind as soon as I see your gesture.

I hold the defusal manual. According to it:
- Green light $\rightarrow$ cut blue wire (Wire 2)
- Orange light $\rightarrow$ cut yellow wire (Wire 3)
- White light $\rightarrow$ cut green wire (Wire 1)
- The light changes every round, cycling through green, orange, and white.
- What matters is the light color at the exact moment of the cut.

Currently:
- In Round 1, the light was white.
- The turn order in every round is: Mute $\rightarrow$ Blind $\rightarrow$ Deaf.
- If I gesture a wire number to Deaf now (Round 2), Deaf will see it at the end of Round 2 and instruct Blind. Blind would then execute the cut at the start of Round 3.
- In Round 3, the light will not be white, and because we do not yet know the direction of the 3-color cycle (whether white leads to green or orange), guessing which wire to cut in Round 3 would be a 50/50 gamble.
- By waiting in Round 2, Deaf will observe and report the light's new color for Round 2, establishing the exact cycle sequence. Moreover, any cycle of length 3 returns to its Round 1 state (white) in Round 4. In Round 3, I can safely gesture ☝ (Wire 1 / green wire), Deaf will convey it at the end of Round 3, and Blind will cut Wire 1 in Round 4 under the white light.

Therefore, I will wait this round.

```
wait()
```

TURN 3
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
The light never holds. It changes every round, and it always walks the
same circle of three colours. What matters is what it shows at the
moment of the cut.

| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| green | blue |
| orange | yellow |
| white | green |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: UPDATE: The bomb light just changed from WHITE to ORANGE! Display is still 0. Wires remain 1: green, 2: blue, 3: yellow. Mute: Blind cannot see gestures and I cannot hear speech. Please gesture to me (☝ for Wire 1, ✌ for Wire 2, 🤟 for Wire 3, or 👍 for confirm / button) so I can speak instructions to Blind!

I know from the manual that the bomb's light cycles through three colors every round: green, orange, and white. The observed light sequence was White in Round 1 and Orange in Round 2, meaning the cycle is White $\rightarrow$ Orange $\rightarrow$ Green $\rightarrow$ White.

In Round 3, Deaf goes after Blind, so any instruction Deaf speaks in Round 3 will reach Blind in time for Blind to act in Round 4. In Round 4, the light will return to White. According to the manual, under a White light, the Green wire must be cut. Wire 1 is Green.

I will gesture ☝ to Deaf so Deaf can instruct Blind to cut Wire 1.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["☝"])
```

TURN 4
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
The light never holds. It changes every round, and it always walks the
same circle of three colours. What matters is what it shows at the
moment of the cut.

| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| green | blue |
| orange | yellow |
| white | green |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Mute: Deaf cannot hear anything, only see gestures. If you know what to do based on Display 0, orange light, and wires (1: green, 2: blue, 3: yellow), gesture to Deaf using their symbols so Deaf can speak the instruction to me.
Deaf says: Blind: Mute just gestured ☝! That means cut Wire 1 (the first wire)! Also note: the light is currently green and display is 0.

I have confirmed that the light cycle is White (Round 1) $\rightarrow$ Orange (Round 2) $\rightarrow$ Green (Round 3) $\rightarrow$ White (Round 4). Deaf has already instructed Blind to cut Wire 1. In this round (Round 4), Blind acts immediately after me, when the light will be White. Under a White light, cutting Wire 1 (the green wire) is the correct action according to the manual. I will wait.

```
wait()
```
